verdict.root_cause: At 11:36:49 the ad service's JVM shut down cleanly and went permanently silent, with no startup banner afterward [tr_fb19c68442da]. One second later platform-automation re-applied the 2.2.0-ad-hotfix.2 image to the ad workload — the third application of the same artifact in 45 minutes after two reverts [tr_c52b7cd59488]. The replacement never produced a log line, so the ad endpoint ceased to exist on the network. Frontend's sole repeating failure is gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE / EHOSTUNREACH to 172.18.0.28:9555, sustained for ~22 minutes against a single peer [tr_977423efbb09], and the one errored sampled trace terminates at frontend -> AdService/GetAds and propagates up through frontend-proxy [tr_49f6226042e9]. Ad's metrics show 53 intervals with no traffic at all versus zero in baseline [tr_0525bcf2e66e]. Frontend itself has no changes and no error-ratio departure [tr_a6a241f1c862, tr_19c620a8156d], so it is the reporter, not the culprit.
verdict.reasoning: Ad's self-reported graceful shutdown at 11:36:49 and the image re-application at 11:36:50 coincide to the second [tr_fb19c68442da, tr_c52b7cd59488]. No startup line follows, so the newly applied artifact is not running — the running artifact is not the one that should be running. A crash or OOM would have preempted the shutdown hooks and left a trace; none exists [tr_fb19c68442da]. With no process bound to the ad address, frontend's connect attempts fail at the transport layer against exactly one peer and port, with no recovery [tr_977423efbb09], and the trace pins that hop to AdService/GetAds [tr_49f6226042e9]. Ad's metric traffic gaps are the same absence seen from the metrics side [tr_0525bcf2e66e]. Fixing it means rolling the image reference back to the last version that actually ran and stopping the automation loop that keeps re-applying the hotfix tag.
open_questions: Nothing observed the ad workload's orchestration state after 11:36:50 — whether the hotfix image failed to pull, crashed pre-logging, or was never scheduled is unconfirmed; the verdict rests on absence of logs.
The mapping of 172.18.0.28:9555 to ad is inferred from the port and the trace endpoint, not confirmed against service discovery.

Frontend's error ratio is flat and only 1 of 10 traces errored, yet severity is critical; the product-reviews and product-catalog latency signals [tr_49f6226042e9] were never dispatched against and may be a separate fault.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad pod is running but network-isolated, so frontend cannot reach it.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned-but-running process would still log and complain about unreachable peers; ad logged a clean shutdown and then nothing [tr_fb19c68442da], with an image change landing one second later [tr_c52b7cd59488].

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix ad container started but was killed or starved on startup, leaving the endpoint down.
alternatives.why_not: No OOM, fatal-signal, or restart-loop evidence appears, and no subsequent startup attempt was logged at all [tr_fb19c68442da]; the artifact flapping [tr_c52b7cd59488] is the better-supported mechanism.
